page.title: Digital Run of Show Planning Guide
page.description: Learn the decisions, checklist items, tool categories and rehearsal steps that make a digital run of show reliable and repeatable for webinars and hybrid events.
page.h1: What is a digital run of show and how do you build one?
page.definition: A digital run of show is a timed, cue‑by‑cue document that maps every segment, speaker, graphic, video roll and backup path for a virtual or hybrid event so the producer, platform operator and moderators execute the same plan in real time.
page.quick_answer: Assign a single owner for the run of show, lock the platform and rehearsal dates, and create a backup stream before the first speaker goes live.

sections.h2: Who owns the digital run of show and what decisions must be made first?

blocks.p: A single producer or show caller should own the run of show and decide the audience outcome, format, platform and backup strategy before any speaker is confirmed. This ownership prevents duplicated cues and missed hand‑offs during the live event.

sections.h2: What checklist items belong in every digital run of show?

blocks.p: Every run of show must contain timed cues, speaker slots, graphic and video rolls, Q&A windows, backup cues and a sign‑off column for each owner. The list below captures the minimum viable sequence.

sections.h2: Which tool categories support run‑of‑show creation and rehearsal?

blocks.p: Four tool categories cover planning, documentation, live production and backup streaming. Selecting one tool per category keeps the workflow simple and auditable.

sections.h2: How do you structure rehearsals and backup readiness?

blocks.p: Run a full rehearsal on the actual platform two to five days before the event and a technical check sixty minutes before going live, then verify the backup stream is recording. sections.h2: When should you hand off the final run of show to the production crew?

blocks.p: Deliver the locked run of show to the producer, platform operator and moderator at least one day before the event so each owner can confirm cues and backup triggers. Early hand‑off reduces last‑minute changes that break the cue sheet.

faq.q: What is the minimum lead time to build a reliable digital run of show?
faq.a: A reliable run of show needs at least two to three weeks from approved brief to live date, giving time for speaker briefs, rehearsal, backup testing and sign‑off. Repeat formats can compress the schedule but still require a full rehearsal and technical check.

faq.q: Which roles are essential for a webinar versus a hybrid summit?
faq.a: A simple webinar can be managed by a single producer who handles cues, chat and backup. A hybrid summit adds a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator to cover stage transitions, on‑site AV coordination and the redundant streaming.

faq.q: How do you verify the backup stream works before going live?
faq.a: During the technical check sixty minutes before start, push the same program feed to the backup encoder and confirm the recording is clean, audio levels match and the failover switch activates without viewer interruption and that the backup URL is reachable by the moderator team.

faq.q: What deliverables should you expect from a production partner for a digital run of show?
faq.a: A production partner should deliver the run of show document, speaker brief and rehearsal schedule, branded slide template with lower thirds, a live producer on the day, Q&A moderation, a tested backup stream, and an edited recording plus short clips for replay distribution.
